subject: Scenario matrix: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC — post-demo recap
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Perez <alex@cyclehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Oct 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps from today’s demo — deployment-mode scenarios

Hi Alex — great to meet the team today, thanks for the demo walkthrough. Per our call, I wanted to capture the three deployment paths we discussed and outline the inputs we need to build a scenario matrix and pricing comparison: hosted API (pay-per-token), Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), and Private VPC (customer-managed, optional on-prem).

Summary of tradeoffs (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding, no infra commitments. Best for variable volume or proof-of-concept. Cost = per-token + minor request charges.
- Dedicated: lower per-token unit economics at scale, predictable latency and throughput. Requires monthly/annual commit (reserved GPUs).
- Private VPC / On-prem: full network/data control and compliance alignment; higher operational lift and either a subscription or bring-your-own-infra pricing.

What we need from you to produce apples-to-apples numbers:
1) Estimated 90-day and 12-month token volumes (prompt + generation). If uncertain, give best/likely/worst.
2) Typical request profile: tokens per request, average response length, concurrency or peak QPS, latency SLO (P50/P95).
3) Any hard constraints: data residency (e.g., must stay in us-east), required certifications (SOC2/ISO), or procurement cadence (SOW/PO lead times).
4) Expected go-live target and desired procurement path (self-serve / PO / committed reserved).

Deliverables from our side: I’ll build a scenario matrix with: cost/month under per-token vs reserved commit for three volume tiers, break-even commit level, and a short draft quote for procurement that outlines delta to a 12-month reserved commitment. Expect that by Monday EOD I’ll send an initial spreadsheet and a short note explaining the assumptions.

Next steps: if you can reply with the bullets above (rough numbers are totally fine), I’ll prioritize the matrix for your review. Also tagging Vivek and Marcus to weigh in on quantization/instance suggestions for Dedicated vs Private.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi — good summary and yes, the three paths map to our internal tradeoffs. Quick answers below (rough estimates):

1) Volume: 90-day estimated tokens = 120M (best 80M / likely 120M / worst 40M). 12-month run rate if we scale = ~1.2B tokens.
2) Request profile: average request ~120 input tokens, ~300 output tokens. Expected peak concurrency 30 QPS, steady-state 7–12 QPS. Target latency P50 < 150ms, P95 < 350ms for UX-critical flows.
3) Constraints: All PHI must remain in us-east. SOC2 is required; we'll need an indemnity clause for data handling in contract. Procurement prefers PO for hosted; reserved commit needs legal review.
4) Go-live: pilot in the next 8–10 weeks; production in Q2 next year. Procurement lead time ~4–6 weeks for PO approvals.

Anything else you need, let us know — I can pull more granular telemetry if it helps.

—Alex

Subject: Scenario matrix and preliminary cost examples (attached)

Alex — attaching the scenario matrix (redwood_scenario_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a short preview quote (quote_reserved_commit_preview.pdf). Key assumptions are called out in the spreadsheet; highlight below for quick reading.

Quick highlights (using your likely numbers: 120M tokens / 30 QPS peaks):
- Hosted API: ~ $2,400 / month (token pricing example: $0.002 / 1k tokens for generation tier used in this calc). This is easiest to spin up for pilot; no commit.
- Dedicated (reserved monthly commit): at 120M tokens/month the break-even commit is approximately a 3 x reduction in $/1k token vs hosted once you reserve a medium GPU pool for p95 latency targets. Example: reserved 4-GPU pool (shared across services) estimated $10k/month commit; effective token cost depends on util.
- Private VPC: premium for private control + optional on-prem. Expect higher baseline platform fee (~$8k–$12k/mo) plus either a reduced per-token or OEM pricing if you bring infra. Best fit if you need strict residency and long-term control.

Notes on break-even math (brief):
- We modelled generation cost by mapping throughput (tokens/sec) to GPU hours using our kernel-level profiling for your request size and target latency. Then we amortized reserved instance monthly cost across expected usable hours.
- For conservative planning, we assume 65% utilization on reserved pools (since spikes need headroom); if CycleHealth can commit to auto-scaling policies to push utilization to 80%+, reserved economics improve materially.

Ask: if you can confirm whether you prefer a provider-manage (Redwood-managed Dedicated) or an infra-managed Dedicated (we spin up capacity in your cloud account), I’ll produce two committed quotes. Procurement, feel free to confirm PO timing and any SOW/legal requirements we should pre-populate.

Attachments: redwood_scenario_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB), quote_reserved_commit_preview.pdf (PDF, 28KB)

Best,
